customerSupportCode.name: X-Customer-Support-Code
customerSupportCode.description: Per-intent support code returned at intent creation (for example `BRIJ-K7MQ-T9RV`). Authorizes reading the airline order and filing a refund request. Not a payment credential.

brijSponsoredPreview.name: X-BRIJ-SPONSORED-SIGNATURE
brijSponsoredPreview.description: BRIJ gateway Ed25519 signature for sponsored preview calls. The signature covers version, timestamp, wallet address, method, host, path, and request body hash.

authorSession.description: Bearer token from POST /recipes/session, scoped to recipe authorship.

IntentID.name: intent_id
IntentID.description: The intent id returned when the intent was created.

origin_iata.description: Departure airport or city IATA code, 3 letters (e.g. MAD).

destination_iata.description: Arrival airport or city IATA code, 3 letters (e.g. LIS).

return_date.description: Optional. Adds the inbound slice (destination back to origin on this date). Round-trip offers cover both directions and are booked in ONE /air/book — the escrow amount is the round-trip total.

adults.description: Adult passengers, 1 to 9 (the airline maximum per booking). The offer is priced for this many travellers, and /air/book must later supply exactly this many passengers.

limit.description: Optional. Cap the number of offers returned; 0 or absent returns every match. Offers are sorted per `sort` (cheapest first by default), so a limit keeps the best ones under that order. ONE EXCEPTION, and it is why the array can hold limit+1 rows: when the cut would have dropped the cheapest NONSTOP, that offer is appended as the last row, so a page never hides that a direct exists even from a caller that reads no other field. It is appended, never inserted at its price rank — the first `limit` rows are still the `limit` best under your sort, and offers[0] is still the cheapest. `highlights` names it too.

cheapest_per_itinerary.description: Optional. Return only the cheapest fare of each physical itinerary (comparison_key); the folded fares stay visible in each offer's fare_options (offer_id, brand, price, refundable, changeable, checked bags), so refundability questions are answerable from the grouped data itself. Recommended for LLM-driven agents together with limit.

sort.description: Ordering, ascending only. Default price. duration = fastest first, departure = earliest local departure first, emissions = lowest CO2 first (unknown values sort last). nonstop_first = every nonstop itinerary (price-ascending) before any connection — with a limit, directs survive the cut.

max_stops.description: Maximum plane changes PER DIRECTION: 0 keeps directs only (a round trip qualifies only if both legs are direct). Absent = any. Technical stops without a plane change do not count.

departure_after.description: Outbound departs at or after this time, LOCAL to the departure airport, HH:MM.

departure_before.description: Outbound departs at or before this time, local HH:MM. Combine with departure_after for a window: afternoon = after 12:00, before 18:00.

max_price.description: Decimal cap on total_amount in the offer currency, e.g. "250.00".

search_id.description: Capability token for POST /air/search-updates. The search answers fast with the quick fulfillers' offers; slower tiers keep adding offers for a couple of minutes, and this token reads them as they land. Unguessable; expires ~5 minutes after the search. Treat it like a secret.

status.description: "complete" when every fulfiller tier has finished quoting; "enriching" while slower tiers are still adding offers — poll /air/search-updates to receive them.

poll_after_ms.description: Suggested delay before the next /air/search-updates poll. Absent when the search is complete.

next.description: Present while status is enriching: what to do, in words — keep polling /air/search-updates until complete before choosing. Absent when complete.

matched_count.description: How many offers survived the filters and grouping BEFORE the limit cut — what a full listing would hold.

SearchHighlights.description: The three offers an agent asks about first — cheapest, fastest, cheapest nonstop — each taken from EVERYTHING that matched, before the limit cut. A page of the 15 cheapest is only honest if it says what it left out: on a long-haul route every one of the 15 cheapest can be a connection while a direct exists at a higher price. Read cheapest_nonstop before concluding a route has no direct flight. A field is absent when no offer qualifies (no nonstop on the route, or none within max_stops / the time window).

offer_id.description: Bookable like any other offer (POST /air/offer-details, then /air/intents), whether or not it appears in offers.

total_amount_decimal.description: The price a buyer pays for this offer — what POST /air/intents asks as expected_escrow_amount.

duration.description: Whole journey, every direction summed, ISO 8601.

stops.description: Total plane changes across every direction; 0 = nonstop both ways.

departing_at.description: Local departure of the first segment.

origin_iata.description: Start of the whole journey (first leg's origin).

destination_iata.description: End of the whole journey (last leg's destination), NOT the first connection point.

departing_at.description: Journey departure, airport-local time with no UTC offset.

arriving_at.description: FINAL arrival at the journey destination, airport-local time with no UTC offset.

origin_time_zone.description: IANA timezone of the journey origin.

destination_time_zone.description: IANA timezone of the journey destination.

stops.description: Number of connections. 0 means a direct flight.

technical_stops.description: Refuelling-type stops across all legs, without plane change. Truly non-stop = stops 0 and technical_stops 0.

segments.description: Every leg of the itinerary, in order.

comparison_key.description: Identifies the physical itinerary: offers with the SAME comparison_key are the same flights at different fares or sellers. Group by it to deduplicate results (a search commonly returns 100+ offers for a few dozen itineraries).

fare_brand_name.description: Airline's name for this fare (e.g. "Basic", "Flexible Balearic"). The SAME flight is listed once per fare and per seller: use this plus conditions, baggage and owner_name to tell same-flight offers apart. Empty when the airline did not name the fare.

cabin_class.description: Normalized cabin: economy, premium_economy, business, first. Empty when unknown.

cabin_class_marketing_name.description: The airline's own name for the cabin.

checked_bags_included.description: Checked bags included for the WHOLE journey (minimum across legs). null = the airline did not say — do not assume 0.

carry_on_bags_included.description: Carry-on bags included for the whole journey. null = unknown.

conditions.description: Change/refund permissions for this fare; null when the airline disclosed nothing.

fare_options_count.description: Present only on cheapest_per_itinerary searches: how many fares of this same itinerary were collapsed into this cheapest one.

fare_options.description: Present on cheapest_per_itinerary searches: EVERY fare of this itinerary (this offer included), cheapest first. The grouped view is lossless on price, brand, refund/change conditions and checked bags — never claim such a fare does not exist without reading this list.

slices.description: Each direction of the journey: one entry for a one-way, two for a round trip (outbound then inbound). The journey-level fields above describe the OUTBOUND for compatibility; slices is the canonical and only complete view for round trips. comparison_key joins all directions, so two round trips sharing an outbound but not a return stay distinct.

total_emissions_kg.description: Estimated CO2 for the journey, decimal kilograms. Empty when the provider does not report it. Varies several-fold between offers on the same route.

identity_documents_required.description: true = this fare demands passenger identity documents, which this API cannot collect: POST /air/intents refuses such offers with 409 identity_documents_not_supported. Filter them out before choosing.

supported_loyalty_programmes.description: IATA codes of airline loyalty programmes this offer can credit miles to (e.g. BA, AF, UA). Empty when none or unknown.

base_amount_decimal.description: Fare before tax; total = base + tax.

total_amount.description: Atomic amount used by the API for money comparisons.

funding_wallet.description: Solana wallet expected to fund the escrow.

refund_wallet.description: Optional Solana wallet for refunds. Defaults to funding_wallet.

offer_id.description: The offer to book, sent back EXACTLY as received from POST /air/search or POST /air/offer-details — never reassembled by hand.

BookingIntentView.description: Read-only projection of a booking intent. Omits customer_support_code and passenger PII; those fields are returned once at intent-creation and /book time.

passenger_count.description: How many passengers the offer was priced for; /air/book must supply exactly this many.

booking_reference.description: The airline PNR, present once the ticket is issued (Duffel: when the order is paid; browser tiers: when the supplier's ticket email arrives, which can take a few hours). Show it to the traveller: it is what they check in with. Poll this endpoint until it appears; no other call is needed.

passenger_count.description: How many passengers the offer was priced for; /air/book must supply exactly this many.

PassengerInput.description: Passenger details. Field constraints mirror the upstream airline contract; values the airline would reject (e.g. gender other than 'm'/'f') are rejected by this API before settling x402, so funds stay in the agent's wallet on validation failure.

given_name.description: Given (first) name as on the travel document.

family_name.description: Family (last) name as on the travel document.

title.description: Honorific. Lowercase, exactly one of the allowed values.

gender.description: Biological sex as recorded on the travel document. Lowercase, exactly 'm' or 'f' (the airline does not accept other values).

email.description: Contact email. Receives booking-in-progress and booking-confirmed notifications.

phone_number.description: Phone number in E.164 format (leading '+', country code, no spaces or punctuation).

nationality.description: REQUIRED for trip.com: offers, ignored otherwise. Passenger nationality as a country name in English, e.g. "France" — the supplier's booking form demands the travel document up front.

passport_number.description: REQUIRED for trip.com: offers, ignored otherwise. Passport or national ID number.

passport_expiry.description: REQUIRED for trip.com: offers, ignored otherwise. Document expiry, YYYY-MM-DD, must be in the future. Missing/expired documents are refused BEFORE payment (400 travel_document_required / travel_document_expired).

passengers.description: Exactly as many passengers as the intent's passenger_count (= adults searched), LEAD PASSENGER FIRST. Positions map to the offer's travellers. The lead passenger receives all emails, and refund requests authenticate against the LEAD passenger's family name. Duplicate travellers (same name and birth date) are refused with 400 duplicate_passenger. All refunds are all-or-nothing: one booking = one escrow, there is no per-passenger cancellation.

OfferSegment.description: One flight leg of an offer. Times are in the airport's local timezone and carry no UTC offset.

origin_time_zone.description: IANA timezone of the origin airport; combine with departing_at for an absolute instant.

destination_time_zone.description: IANA timezone of the destination airport; combine with arriving_at for an absolute instant.

duration.description: Leg duration, ISO 8601 (e.g. PT1H15M). Precomputed — never subtract the naive local timestamps.

marketing_carrier_name.description: Airline SELLING this leg. Differs from carrier_name (the operating airline) on codeshares — e.g. sold by British Airways, operated by Iberia Express. Explains same-flight offers priced differently by seller.

carrier_iata.description: IATA code of the operating airline (carrier_name) — the stable identifier where the name is a display string.

marketing_carrier_iata.description: IATA code of the selling airline (marketing_carrier_name).

operating_flight_number.description: Operating carrier's own flight number; flight_number is the marketed one shown on the boarding pass.

fare_basis_code.description: Airline fare basis identifier for this leg.

technical_stops.description: Refuelling-type stops on this leg WITHOUT a plane change. A leg with technical stops is still one segment; truly non-stop means stops == 0 AND technical_stops == 0.

technical_stop_airports.description: IATA codes of the technical-stop airports, in order.

FareConditions.description: What the fare permits before departure. Every field of the parent offer is emitted; null on an *_allowed field means the airline did not disclose it — treat as unknown, do NOT assume false. Penalty amounts are decimal strings in the given currency; "0" means free.

change_allowed.description: true = changeable (see penalty), false = not changeable, null = airline did not say.

change_penalty_amount.description: Decimal fee to change, "0" = free change. Absent when unknown.

refund_allowed.description: true = refundable before departure (see penalty), false = non-refundable, null = airline did not say.

refund_penalty_amount.description: Decimal fee to refund, "0" = free refund. Absent when unknown.

OfferService.description: One purchasable ancillary on an offer. INFORMATIONAL ONLY: services cannot be bought through this API — use these prices to compare a bare fare plus a paid bag against a fare that already includes one.

baggage_type.description: For baggage services: checked or carry_on.

total_amount_decimal.description: Price PER UNIT of the service.

offer.description: The offer re-fetched live: total_amount and expires_at are CURRENT, unlike a minutes-old search result.

available_services.description: Purchasable extras with prices. Empty array = the airline offers none on this fare (an answer, not missing data).

OfferSlice.description: One direction of the journey: the outbound, and for round trips the inbound. Same semantics as the journey-level fields (whole-direction endpoints, airport-local times, stops = plane changes).

checked_bags_included.description: Checked bags included on THIS direction (minimum across its legs; null when a leg does not report it). A round trip can mix brands per direction, and the journey-level checked_bags_included is then the minimum of the two.

OfferFareOption.description: Compact form of one fare inside a grouped result: enough to answer refundability, changeability, baggage and price questions without another search, and to act on the fare via its offer_id. refundable/changeable keep the null-means-undisclosed semantics.

change_penalty_amount.description: Fee the airline states for a change before departure, when changeable = true and a fee is disclosed (e.g. "190.00"). Absent when free, unknown, or not changeable.

refund_penalty_amount.description: Fee the airline states for a refund before departure, when refundable = true and a fee is disclosed. Absent when free, unknown, or non-refundable.

directions.description: Round trips only: the brand and checked allowance of each direction in order (outbound, inbound). This is what differs between "Standard Economy / Basic Economy" and "Basic Economy / Standard Economy" at the same price — the journey-level checked_bags_included is the minimum of the two. Absent on one-ways and on browser-tier menus.

cabin.description: browser tier only: cabin label from the supplier's fare menu.

seats_left.description: browser tier only: seats remaining at this fare, when the supplier discloses it.

conditions.description: browser tier only: the supplier's verbatim condition notes (baggage, refund policy).

fare_index.description: browser tier only: the fare's position in the supplier's menu - the index the book flow selects. The row's offer_id embeds it.

status.description: "complete" once no further offers can arrive.

offers.description: The FULL merged offer list so far (not a delta), deduplicated across fulfiller tiers, shaped exactly like the original search request.

matched_count.description: How many offers survived the filters and grouping BEFORE the limit cut — what a full listing would hold.

new_since_last_poll.description: How many offers landed since the previous poll (all of them on the first poll).

poll_after_ms.description: Suggested delay before the next poll. Absent when complete.

next.description: Present while status is enriching: keep polling until complete before choosing. Absent when complete.

journey_id.description: Send it back EXACTLY to POST /rail/quote.

price_from.description: The merchant's own price, in merchant_currency.

total_from.description: ALL-IN price in USDC (conversion + fee included).

adults.description: Travellers searched; the buy names exactly this many.

pending_merchants.description: Merchants still searching (retry the same request).

above_limit.description: Journeys hidden because their total is above the per-order limit.

offer_id.description: Pass it to POST /rail/intents, exactly as received. Valid ~20 min (expires_at).

product.description: What is being bought, as the merchant names it.

breakdown.description: What the merchant itself charges (items, shipping, tax), in merchant_currency.

fx.description: When the merchant is not USD: ECB rate, conversion margin, merchant_usd.

total_amount.description: ALL-IN price in USDC: the escrow amount.

requires.description: What the buy must provide (person, document, contact.phone…).

ship_countries.description: Instant quotes: the countries ship_to.country may be (ISO 3166 alpha-2). One entry for a store whose domain names its country (amazon.de); every euro-area country for a euro store whose domain names none (on.com); absent when the store's country is unknown, in which case the buyer names it.

ship_country.description: The single country this order ships to, or for a multi-market store the market its product link named (a default the buyer may change within ship_countries).

merchant_order_number.description: The merchant's order number / booking reference.

status.description: purchasing: the merchant is being paid; follow with the orders endpoint.

location.description: A city name, when no city_id or coordinates are sent.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place, with longitude, instead of a city.

check_out_date.description: Check-out day, YYYY-MM-DD, at most 30 nights later.

child_ages.description: One age per child, up to 4.

free_cancellation_only.description: Only hotels with a free-cancellation rate.

stars.description: Keep hotels with one of these star ratings, e.g. [4, 5]. Unrated hotels are left out when set.

sort.description: Order by the all-in total: price (default, cheapest first) or price_desc. Applied before the 50-hotel cap.

accommodation_id.description: Search ONE hotel: an accommodation_id from GET /hotels/places (hotels[]), instead of a place.

intent_id.description: The intent id returned by POST /hotels/intents.

guests.description: The lead guest first (the reservation's name and the identity for a cancellation), then at least one guest per room.

email.description: The lead guest's email: the confirmation goes there.

special_requests.description: Forwarded to the hotel (early check-in, cot).

hotels.description: Cheapest first: hotel_id, name, rating, review_score, address, distance_km, price_from, total_from (ALL-IN), due_at_hotel_from, currency.

room_types.description: Each room: name, beds, rates[] (rate_id, board, refundable, refundability, cancellation_timeline, price).

price.description: hotel_total (tax and fees included), service_fee, total_amount (ALL-IN, what the escrow holds), due_at_hotel_amount.

status.description: awaiting_payment, booking, confirmed, failed, cancelled, refunded.

info.title: BRIJ Travel API
info.description:
Payments for AI agents: flights (/air/*), trains and long-distance buses
(/rail/*, buses with mode=bus) and hotels (/hotels/*), paid per call with x402
in USDC on Solana, with escrow-backed booking and automatic refunds.

`POST /air/search` accepts either a valid x402 `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` or a
BRIJ gateway sponsored-preview signature. `POST /air/intents`,
`POST /air/book`, and `POST /air/refund-requests` are protected by x402.
Clients that do not send a valid `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header receive
`402 Payment Required` with a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header and JSON payment
requirements body.

Action endpoints (POST /air/book, POST /air/refund-requests) take intent_id
in the request body — never in the path. The two reads are path-addressed:
GET /air/intents/{intent_id} and GET /air/orders/{order_id}.

**What a booking costs.** The flight's price is ONE figure: an offer's total_amount, which is exactly the expected_escrow_amount POST /air/book pays (booking fee included). The x402 calls around it are billed separately, each on its own: /air/search 0.10 USDC (more under load), /air/offer-details 0.01 (0.10 on a browser tier), /air/intents 0.10, /air/orders 0.01. So a wallet's total spend is the escrow amount plus a few tenths — e.g. 775.72 escrow + 0.10 intent + 2 × 0.10 searches = 776.02 USDC. When quoting the traveller a price, quote the escrow amount and say the call fees are separate.
info.x-guidance:
Four steps, each paid per call with x402 (USDC on Solana).

1. POST /air/search — find live offers. Price is dynamic: 0.10 USDC x1..50 depending on load, so always read the current PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge rather than reusing a price you saw earlier.
2. POST /air/intents — lock one offer_id and derive its escrow. Costs 0.10 USDC. The response carries the intent id, the customer_support_code (PERSIST BOTH — the support code cannot be re-read later and is required to read the order or request a refund) and passenger_count: how many passengers /air/book must supply.
3. POST /air/book — send intent_id and exactly passenger_count passengers in the body, LEAD PASSENGER FIRST (the lead receives all emails and is the identity for refund requests; duplicate travellers are refused). The price is this intent's escrow amount, i.e. the ticket total for all passengers, quoted in the challenge. Booking is asynchronous: a 200 means the request was accepted, then poll GET /air/intents/{intent_id} until status is booked or refunded.
4. POST /air/refund-requests — optional, 0.10 USDC. Needs intent_id in the body plus the X-Customer-Support-Code header and X-Passenger-Family-Name: the LEAD passenger's family name. It files a request for manual review; it does not execute a refund.

Action POSTs never take an id in the path: send intent_id in the request body of POST /air/book and POST /air/refund-requests. The two GET reads (GET /air/intents/{intent_id}, GET /air/orders/{order_id}) are path-addressed. If the upstream price moved between steps 2 and 3 the booking is rejected and the escrow is refunded automatically to the refund wallet frozen at intent creation.

To drill into one offer (fresh price/expiry, paid-ancillary prices such as extra bags), POST /air/offer-details with the offer_id — cheaper than re-searching. Seat maps and legal fare-rule text remain unobtainable: when a decision depends on them, say so to the customer rather than guessing.

Never answer "no fare with property X exists" from a truncated ungrouped search: pricier variants (refundable, with bags, higher cabin) sort to the tail and fall off. Use cheapest_per_itinerary=true and read fare_options.

get.description: Free, no auth. Aggregate carrier catalog over every fulfiller tier: source "api" is the API-settled (Duffel) catalog, refreshed at most daily; a tier name ("trip.com" = the OTA, "ryanair.com" = ryanair.com) means that fulfiller has actually QUOTED the carrier — observed coverage that grows with searches and understates an OTA's true span. Presence is recognition, not a bookability promise: what is bookable for a route is what POST /air/search returns.

sources.description: "api" and/or fulfiller tier names that quoted the carrier

post.summary: Pay the escrow and request booking.

price.note: the price IS the intent's expected_escrow_amount — the fare held in escrow, not a fee

post.description:
The intent id travels in the request body; the resource URL is static. Paid x402 endpoint. The payment challenge is dynamic for the intent:
`payTo` is the intent escrow address, `asset` is the expected escrow
mint, and `amount` is the expected escrow amount.

After x402 settlement, the API records the passenger list (lead first), verifies exact
escrow funding on-chain, and enqueues the booking worker. Airline payment
and escrow capture happen asynchronously.

If booking fails after x402 settlement, retry the same `/book` call;
excess funds remain refundable to `refund_wallet`.

**Lowcost travel document.** For an intent created on a trip.com: offer, each passenger additionally requires nationality, passport_number, and passport_expiry (YYYY-MM-DD, in the future) — the supplier's booking form demands them. Missing or expired documents are refused BEFORE payment (400 travel_document_required / travel_document_expired). Booking is asynchronous exactly like fastbooking: poll GET /air/intents/{intent_id} until booked or refunded. A browser-tier booking is captured only once the airline actually issues the ticket, and auto-refunds if it never does.

409.description: Intent is not active, `intent_expired` if its booking window has closed (create a new intent from a fresh offer; detail carries `expired_at`), `offer_expired` if the offer has left the airline's inventory, `offer_repriced` if its live price no longer matches the intent (detail carries `expected_ticket_amount` and `current_ticket_amount`) — both checked live against the airline BEFORE settlement, so the refusal is free — escrow is missing, funding is not exact, or `booking_already_requested` if a prior /book succeeded for this intent (retry has no effect; the worker is processing it).

402.description: x402 payment required or payment verification failed.

501.description: Upstream flight provider is not configured.

503.description: Booking is temporarily disabled by the operator (`booking_disabled`). Existing intents and refund requests are unaffected.

post.summary: Create an escrow-backed booking intent from a selected offer.
post.description:
Paid x402 endpoint. Send a valid `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header to create
the intent. Without payment, the API returns `402 Payment Required`.

Optional request field referrer: an affiliate code — the resolved affiliate wallet is frozen on the intent and credited a share of the platform fee once the booking captures and the journey is flown without refund; unknown or self-referring codes are silently ignored.

Creates the local booking intent and initializes its Solana escrow.
This does not fund the escrow, pay the airline, or issue a ticket.

**Lowcost (trip.com: offers).** These book through a browser-driven fulfiller, not an airline API, so a few rules differ. The escrow amount is the offer's own price (fare menus from POST /air/offer-details are bookable: an offer_id like "trip.com:<flight>##<n>@s<search>" locks fare n and the escrow prices at that fare). A fare offer_id is only bookable while its menu is fresh (~30 min) — a stale one returns 409 fare_menu_expired, re-open the fares and retry. If the most recent fare check (POST /air/offer-details) for the offer failed within the last ~30 min, intent creation returns 409 fare_check_failed — a failed fare check temporarily blocks booking that offer; retry POST /air/offer-details in a few minutes and book once it answers. If that supplier is not currently selling, intent creation returns 409 browser_booking_unavailable — book a fastbooking offer, or retry later. An unknown/expired browser-tier offer_id returns 404 offer_not_found. **Send an offer_id back EXACTLY as received.** A browser-tier id is derived from the flight, so it is the same string for every buyer; the trailing "@s<search>" is what ties it to YOUR search, and therefore to the cabin, the party and the fare menu your price came from. Strip it and the offer resolves against whoever searched that flight most recently. Booking then requires the travel document at POST /air/book (see there).

400.description: Invalid wallet, request body, or payment signature.

402.description: x402 payment required or payment verification failed.

409.description: Offer is unsupported or no longer usable, or an active intent already exists for this funding_wallet and offer_id (code `intent_already_exists`; the existing intent_id is returned in `detail.intent_id`); for browser-tier offers also browser_booking_unavailable, fare_check_failed (a recent fare check failed — retry POST /air/offer-details in a few minutes), fare_menu_expired, or invalid_fare_index.

502.description: Escrow initialization or upstream provider failed.

503.description: Booking is temporarily disabled by the operator (`booking_disabled`). Existing intents and refund requests are unaffected.

get.summary: Fetch a booking intent by id.
get.description: Free. Poll it after /air/book: status moves to booked once the escrow is captured, and booking_reference carries the airline PNR as soon as the ticket is issued. A booking is finished for the traveller when booking_reference is present: relay it to them.

post.summary: Drill into one offer: fare menu, bag prices, live price.
post.description:
Paid x402 endpoint: $0.01 USDC for fastbooking: offers, $0.10 USDC for offers from a browser tier (trip.com:, ryanair:) — reading their fare menu costs a real browser session at the supplier — the PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge always quotes the applicable price.

fastbooking: offers — re-fetches the offer from the flight provider and returns it in the same shape as search results, with CURRENT price and expires_at, plus available_services: the purchasable extras (checked bags with weight limits and prices) on that exact fare. fare_options lists EVERY fare of this flight (same aircraft, every brand: Basic, Standard, Flex…), fresh from the supplier and price-ascending, each with its own bookable offer_id — including fares the search left out of its page. Pick the row you want and pass its offer_id to POST /air/intents.

browser-tier offers (trip.com:, ryanair:) — return the offer with fare_options filled from the supplier's own fare menu: per fare, the price, cabin, seats_left, and conditions[] (the supplier's verbatim wording for baggage allowances and refund policy — {type, text} pairs such as CARRY_ON, CONSIGN, UN_REFUND). Each fare row carries its own bookable offer_id ('<tier>:<flight>##<n>', e.g. 'trip.com:2026-11-07T20:35|2026-11-07T21:55|FR##1') and fare_index: create the intent on that offer_id to book THAT fare - the escrow prices at the fare, and the fulfiller selects the same menu index at the supplier. The fare menu must be fresh (re-drill after ~30 min: 409 fare_menu_expired). Expect 20-45s on a cold read; 202 fares_pending means the menu is still being fetched and nothing was charged — wait for the Retry-After header (15s) and send the same request again: it returns the finished result. Do not treat a 202 as the offer. Results are cached ~5 min per offer_id, so repeats are instant and free of supplier load.

Use it to (1) answer "how much is an extra bag on this fare?" or "is this browser-tier fare refundable?" — the ancillary/conditions questions search results cannot answer — and (2) revalidate a single offer minutes after a search, which is cheaper and quota-friendlier than re-searching.

A stale or unknown offer_id returns 404 and the payment is never settled: refusals cost nothing. Offers expire roughly 20-30 minutes after search; on 404, re-search.

Services are informational only: this API books the fare as-is and cannot add services to the order.

post.summary: Request a manual refund after the intent has been booked.
post.description:
The intent id travels in the request body; the resource URL is static. Paid x402 endpoint. Send a valid `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header to record
the refund request. Without payment, the API returns `402 Payment Required`.

Records a refund request for a booked intent. The on-chain escrow has
already been captured by the time the intent is `booked`, so refunds at
this stage are processed manually by an operator. This endpoint persists
the request and pages the operator on Telegram; the response is
`202 Accepted` and is **not** a guarantee of refund — eligibility and
any applicable carrier penalties are reviewed manually.

For pre-capture states (`active`), the booking_sync worker handles
refunds automatically; this endpoint returns `409 use_automatic_refund`
for those.

The caller must include the `X-Customer-Support-Code` header matching
the code returned at intent creation.


For multi-passenger bookings, X-Passenger-Family-Name is the LEAD passenger's family name (position 0 of the /air/book list).

post.description:
Flight search can be paid with x402 or sponsored by the BRIJ gateway.

For direct x402 clients, send a valid `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Without
payment, the API returns `402 Payment Required` carrying the **current** price.

For BRIJ Wallet preview calls, the gateway may send `X-BRIJ-SPONSORED-*`
headers. Providers should treat that as a BRIJ-sponsored preview, not as a
user-paid x402 settlement.

Every price in the response is the price a buyer pays: total_amount / total_amount_decimal (offers, fare_options, highlights) are all-in, and max_price filters on that figure. POST /air/intents asks exactly this amount as expected_escrow_amount (a wallet enrolled in a fee-waiving cohort is asked less, never more).

Base x402 price is 0.10 USDC. The price is multiplied (up to 50×) by the
current search load: completed searches in the last 60 seconds and
any upstream rate-limit response in the last 5 minutes. Always read
the latest `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` challenge before signing - the price
your client saw a moment ago may already be stale.


The same flight commonly appears several times at different prices: each offer is one fare (fare_brand_name, baggage, change/refund conditions) sold by one seller (owner_name). Two offers on the same flight can share identical conditions and differ only in seller and price — compare the fare fields, never assume cheaper means more restrictive.

**Data boundaries — what this response does and does not contain.**
Each offer carries EVERYTHING the flight inventory provider discloses at search time: itinerary (legs, times with IANA timezones, durations, aircraft, terminals, technical stops), identity (comparison_key, both carriers on codeshares, flight numbers, fare_basis_code), fare content (brand, cabin, included baggage, change/refund conditions with penalties), price breakdown (base + tax), CO2 estimate, and loyalty programmes. To drill into ONE offer — fresh price/expiry and paid-ancillary prices — use POST /air/offer-details. Filters (max_stops, departure_after/before, max_price) apply before sort, grouping and limit — so limit + sort=duration + max_stops=0 means "the fastest directs". Offers default to cheapest first; a full response can exceed 300 KB, so LLM-driven agents should send cheapest_per_itinerary=true with a limit and drill into finalists.

Not available in SEARCH results (use POST /air/offer-details per offer):
- Prices of paid ancillaries (extra checked bags and other extras).
- Seat maps and specific seat availability.
- Full legal fare-rule text. It does not exist upstream in machine form: the structured conditions object IS the complete machine-readable ruleset. For airline-side research, fare_basis_code plus the marketing carrier identifies the exact fare.

Everywhere in this response, null/empty means the airline did not disclose the value — unknown, never zero or false.

**Anti-pattern — truncation without grouping.** cheapest_per_itinerary=false combined with a small limit returns the N cheapest fare INSTANCES, not the N cheapest itineraries. Basic/Lite fares are always cheaper than Comfort/Flex/refundable/business variants of the SAME flight, so the pricier variants sort to the tail and fall off — and their absence from a truncated response proves nothing. To answer "is there a refundable / with-bag / higher-cabin fare?", always use cheapest_per_itinerary=true and read fare_options; it is lossless on price, brand, refund/change conditions and checked bags.

**Progressive results.** The response may carry `status: enriching` plus a `search_id`: slower, cheaper fulfiller tiers are still quoting. Poll the free POST /air/search-updates with that `search_id` (every ~`poll_after_ms`) to receive their offers as they land, until `status: complete` — usually under 2 minutes. Do not choose an offer before then: the slower tiers often carry airlines the fast tier does not (other carriers' nonstops, notably) and cheaper fares. While enriching, the response also says this in words, in `next`.

post.summary: Poll a progressive search for offers still arriving (free).
post.description:
Free companion to POST /air/search — no x402 payment: the search was already paid, and the unguessable `search_id` is the authorization.

A search answers within seconds with the fast tiers' offers and `status: enriching` when slower, cheaper fulfiller tiers are still working. Poll this endpoint (respecting `poll_after_ms`, ~5s) until `status: complete`. Each poll returns the full merged-and-deduplicated offer list so far — idempotent reads, safe to retry.

The `search_id` expires ~5 minutes after the search; after that this endpoint returns 410 and a new search is needed. The rest of the purchase tunnel (offer-details, intents, book) is unchanged — offers gained here are used exactly like offers from the initial response.
